short.en: Merge two numbers in one component

t.en: Back to the grid city: streets only go right or down, and routes to each crossing = up + left. This time the start in the top-left corner already holds a 1 for you, and the robot takes care of the other crossings.

A wire carries just one number. To add up and left together you need a component: the Merger. It has three input dots on top; it adds up whatever is wired in and sends the result out of the dot at its bottom.
For cells in the top row there is no cell above: the view shows “out”, and what comes in is “—”, meaning “there is no road here”. The Merger skips “—” and adds up only real numbers.
Placing a component: drag the Merger from the tray under the board onto an empty slot of the board (a click works too). Hold it to drag it to another slot; drag it back to the tray to remove it.

goal.en: Streets only go right or down, and the start already holds 1. Have the robot work out the number of routes to every crossing: each crossing = up + left.

how.en: Click the “up” and “left” cells in the view, place a Merger, wire both outputs of the View part into it, then wire the Merger to “this cell”.

showcase.en: the first part ever placed on a board: a part sits between the inputs and the output, wires go into its ports and out of its output; a Merger gathers several ways in into one number

body.en: Before, you filled in 12 crossings by hand; now you drew three wires and the robot filled in the whole city.
The 1 at the start was written in for the robot.

note.en: A Merger adds up the numbers its wires bring; “—” is left out.

say.en: Step 1: click “up” and “left” in the view: the “View” part then has two outputs.
Step 2: drag the <part-ref to="part:msum"></part-ref> from the tray onto an empty slot of the board, or just click it.
Step 3: wire each of the View’s two outputs into a dot on the Merger’s left, then wire the Merger’s right-hand dot to “this cell”.

hints.en: Each crossing = up + left: wire both inputs into the same Merger, and the Merger into “this cell”.
